AONL Professional Governance Leadership Conference

PGLC 2027 · June 6–8 · Atlanta

PGLC 2027 Call for Abstracts

Professional governance is more than a structure or committee. It is how nurses leverage influence, demonstrate accountability and create value for patients, organizations, communities and the profession.

Submit an Abstract 2027 Content Priorities

As you consider a submission, think about the stories, challenges, measurable outcomes, lessons learned and innovative approaches that attendees can apply within their own organizations.

We welcome submissions from nurses across roles, specialties, leadership levels and care settings, including APRNs, nurses in ambulatory, community settings, specialty nursing practice, academic partnerships and emerging governance models.

We are particularly interested in experiences that demonstrate how nurses influence practice, participate in decision-making and create meaningful outcomes through professional governance.

2027 Content Priorities

The descriptions and prompts below are intended to spark ideas and illustrate the types of content that align with the goals of PGLC 2027.

01

Professional Governance Demonstrates Value Through Outcomes & Impact

Professional governance creates value when nurses influence decisions and achieve measurable results. We are interested in examples that demonstrate the impact of professional governance on patients, nurses, organizations, communities and the profession.

Ideas to Explore

  • How did nurses use professional governance to improve a clinical, workforce, quality, operational, or financial outcome?
  • How did you measure and demonstrate the value of professional governance?
  • How did professional governance help address a strategic organizational challenge?
  • How did nurses influence decisions that created measurable impact?
  • What factors, conditions, and/or strategies have influenced the function and impact of professional governance?

02

Professional Governance Thrives Through Ownership & Professional Citizenship

Professional governance thrives when nurses embrace ownership of practice, participate in decision-making and accept accountability for outcomes. We are seeking examples that demonstrate how organizations foster professional citizenship and create environments where professional governance can flourish.

Ideas to Explore

  • How did nurses influence a significant practice, policy or operational decision?
  • How did governance structures, councils, or decision-making pathways evolve to become more effective?
  • How did nurses across roles and levels create a culture where professional governance could thrive?
  • How did your organization strengthen ownership of practice, accountability or professional citizenship?
  • How have nurses across specialties, settings or populations advanced governance-driven outcomes?

03

Professional Governance in Practice

Successful professional governance extends beyond councils, committees and structures. We are interested in practical approaches, governance strategies and lessons learned that translate governance principles into meaningful action and impact.

Ideas to Explore

  • How did your organization translate governance principles into meaningful action and impact?
  • What innovative approach improved collaboration, increased nurse influence or accelerated decision-making?
  • How did technology, such has AI and dashboards or other tools strengthen governance processes?
  • How did professional governance influence emerging technologies in nursing practice (i.e., AI, virtual nursing, ambient technologies, etc.)?
  • What lessons learned, challenges or course corrections would benefit other organizations?
